preface.title: About this notebook
preface.para: A familiar path can hold a new story every morning. This little notebook follows two imaginary visits to a riverside garden, with room for observations, sketches, and questions.
The observations and measurements are fictional. The document is an original DocBook sample: headings, contents, lists, tables, code-style notes, and footnotes all come from this XML file.

chapter.title: A morning by the river
chapter.para: At the footbridge, the path divides. One branch follows the water; the other disappears between tall grasses. We take the riverside path and begin with a simple question: what has changed since yesterday?

section.title: Pack light
section.para: A small kit makes it easy to stop and look closely.

listitem.para: A map with the footbridge marked

tip.para: Leave an empty page after each visit for questions that occur to you later.

section.title: Make the first entry

listitem.para: Write the date, time, and starting point.
Choose one detail to describe carefully.
Separate what you saw from what you inferred.

section.para:
A short entry can capture the shape of a whole morning.
A field note can be a sentence, a sketch, or a question. Consistency matters more than length.

example.title: A pocket-sized entry
example.programlisting:
08:10 Footbridge — a thin mist above the water. 08:25 Garden gate — three yellow flowers open. 08:40 Old bench — a feather caught in the grass.
Question: did the flowers open before the mist lifted?

chapter.title: Return to the same place
chapter.para: On the second visit, the sun reaches the garden before we do. Familiar landmarks give the observations a frame, while the details change from one visit to the next.

note.para: A table makes differences easy to scan. Keep the longer descriptions in the journal so the numbers retain their context.

listitem.para: Something recorded directly: a shape, a sound, a count, or a color.
An explanation that might account for an observation.
A reason to return and look again.

blockquote.para: Take home a question as well as a memory.

appendix.title: Before the next visit
appendix.para: Begin again at , then revisit the landmarks in . Add a new page without rewriting the old one; yesterday's uncertainty is part of the story.
